en: Title: *Surūpā-dhāraṇī* Source: Hidas & Szántó Tibetan: D 540 = 1078

Homage to the Tathāgata Surūpa, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. It is as follows: *Oṃ suru suru prasuru prasuru tara tara bhara bhara saṃbhara saṃbhara smara smara saṃtarpaya saṃtarpaya sarvapretānāṃ svāhā*. Having recited this dhāraṇī seven times over food mixed with water, one should snap the fingers three times with the left hand and give it to all the *pretas* in a secluded place. And it should be spoken thus: "May those who seek an opportunity to harm depart; I give this food to the *pretas* dwelling in all world-systems. This must be done before eating. By doing so, a measure (*droṇa*) of rice and food is given to each of all the *pretas*. By acting in this way, one does not become weak nor does one become poor; rather, in birth after birth, one becomes very powerful, gracious, handsome, wealthy, and possessed of great enjoyments; one is long-lived, free from disease, and will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Upon passing away, one is reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. Thus ends the dhāraṇī named Surūpā.
